name: emit_three_pass_draw_sequence
description: Sets a status byte to one, then makes three paired calls in a loop to other routines, emits one extra call with the fixed value 80 when a counter field is zero, and finishes with calls built from the two arguments, one using 200 minus the second argument.

name: init_slot_record_and_draw
description: Writes one 94-byte slot record in a table of three slots, storing a width of 320, a row offset equal to the first argument times 320 (plus 1280 when a flag is set), and the second argument as a coordinate. It then makes draw calls from that offset, repeating one when the second word is non-zero.

name: set_forty_slot_entry_bytes
description: Loops over 40 consecutive entries in a slot table, writing the low byte of the first argument into one byte field and the high byte of the second argument into another byte field in each entry.

name: find_slot_containing_column
description: Stores minus one, scans the three slot records and keeps the index of the last slot whose start and length cover the given position, returning 3 instead when a flag byte is non-zero.

name: scan_slots_for_position_register
description: Scans the three slot records using the position held in a data register and records the index of the slot whose start and length cover it, returning 3 when a flag byte is non-zero. It is the register-argument form of the slot lookup.

name: build_256_entry_bitmask_table
description: Calls one external routine, copies a byte field into a word field, then fills a table of 256 long words where each entry is the OR of the eight longs selected by the set bits of its index.

name: store_pointer_and_mode_three
description: Stores a pointer to a fixed offset inside the game state block into one long field and writes the value 3 into a word field.

name: stub_return_only
description: The body is a bare return with no other instructions, so the routine performs no work when called.

name: initialise_library_resources
description: Makes a chain of calls through a global library base, storing each result, and returns zero as soon as any result is zero. On success it fills a 32-entry word table with identity indices and sentinel values, sets 20 word entries to 200 and sentinels, and returns one.

name: resolve_two_resource_handles
description: Looks up two parameter pairs through a called routine, falling back to a second routine when a lookup returns zero and storing both results in long fields. It then makes two library calls through the global base, stores their results, and issues follow-up calls using those values.

name: store_two_constant_longs
description: Writes two fixed 32-bit constants into consecutive long fields of the state block and does nothing else.

name: advance_two_lfsr_states
description: Steps two state longs with feedback shifts: eight rounds on the first and thirteen on the second, each round shifting left and adding one when bits five and six of the low byte differ. It then calls another routine and returns its result.

name: advance_both_lfsr_states
description: Performs the same two-state feedback shift as its sibling, with the first loop written as a do-while, so eight rounds run on the first state and thirteen on the second. It then calls another routine and returns its result.

name: advance_lfsr_state_thirteen_rounds
description: Runs thirteen feedback-shift rounds on the second state long, where each round shifts left and adds one when bits five and six of the low byte differ, then calls another routine and returns its result.

name: step_position_toward_target
description: Rounds a stored position down to a multiple of eight and clamps it between two limit words. It then moves it by eight toward a target taken from a table indexed by a byte when a mode word is zero, otherwise snaps it straight to the target, and calls a routine when a flag is set and the position changed.

name: clamp_position_and_derive_bounds
description: Clamps a position word to at least 160 and to at most a limit derived from a second word times eight, then stores the position divided by eight, offset by minus 20 and by plus 19, as two bound words.

name: find_record_by_key
description: Walks a chain of variable-length records from a stored cursor or from the given offset, returning the first record whose bytes at offsets four and five match the two-byte key. Returns zero when a record size is zero or the chain ends.

name: update_selection_and_reset_state
description: Runs an update on the currently selected entry, clearing that selection when a flag is set, then refreshes flags for twelve entries and fills a 32-entry identity index table. It also resets the scroll state, and when a condition byte is set it clears a 320-byte buffer and sets the initial limits.

name: reset_scroll_and_indexes
description: Calls a routine for each of thirteen flagged entries, fills a 32-entry identity index table, and resets the scroll state from a byte in the argument block. When a condition byte is set it clears a 320-byte buffer and sets the initial limits.

name: fill_indexes_and_reset
description: Fills a 32-entry identity index table, clears a flag byte, and resets the scroll state from a byte in the argument block. When a condition byte is set it clears a 320-byte buffer and sets the initial limits.

name: select_entry_and_mark_active
description: Sets the active entry index from the low word of the argument, mapping values of 128 or more through a lookup table indexed by the low seven bits, and marks that entry in a flag table. It then clears three state fields when the high byte is zero, or clears the entry's top bit and runs a sequence of calls and a count loop otherwise.

name: select_entry_from_register
description: Marks the entry from a register argument and sets the active entry index from its low word, mapping values of 128 or more through a lookup table. It clears three state fields when the high byte is zero, or clears the entry's top bit and runs calls and a count loop otherwise.

name: store_selection_and_clear_state
description: Stores a byte argument as the current selection and mirrors it into a word field. It clears three state fields when a flag register is zero, or clears the entry's top bit and runs a sequence of calls and a count loop otherwise.

name: clear_top_bit_and_run
description: Clears the top bit of the flag byte for the currently selected entry, makes two calls, and runs a loop with an empty body up to a stored count.

name: spin_until_stored_count
description: Increments a counter until it reaches a stored limit and performs no other work.

name: load_entry_geometry_and_flags
description: Loads the values for the currently selected entry from a table, then derives offsets from them through repeated lookups. For two sub-records it calls a routine when any of four lookups is non-zero, and it finally sets the low bit of a status byte.

name: update_subrecord_pair_status
description: Loops twice over sub-record groups, reading four lookups per group and calling a routine with the entry offset when any lookup is non-zero. It then stores a derived offset and sets the low bit of a status byte.

name: count_records_and_compute_stride
description: Sets the current entry base from a table and walks up to four variable-size records, counting the non-zero ones. It multiplies a stride by that count, makes a call with the product, and writes four words in multiples of the stride.

name: count_records_from_register_base
description: Walks up to four variable-size records starting from a register base, counting the non-zero ones. It multiplies a stride by that count, makes a call with the product, and writes four words in multiples of the stride.

name: write_four_word_multiples
description: Writes four consecutive words holding the low word of the third argument multiplied by zero, one, two and three.

name: run_action_for_matching_slots
description: Loops over entry bytes one through twelve and calls a routine for each entry whose byte equals the current selection byte.

name: run_action_for_matching_entries
description: Performs the same scan of entry bytes one through twelve as its sibling, written as a do-while loop, calling a routine for each entry whose byte equals the current selection byte.

name: load_entry_record_table
description: Loads the record list for the selected entry, storing a count byte and, for each record, the offset and a word from its header. It then matches records to a key word and writes per-record fields such as coordinates, sizes, flags and bit fields into state tables when the count is non-zero.

name: load_record_fields_from_register
description: Performs the record-table loading of its sibling from a register-held offset, skipping the count lookup, and writes the per-record fields for each entry.

name: fill_record_fields_from_offsets
description: Reads one record per entry with a key match, then writes the per-record fields for each entry from its stored offset.

name: resume_record_table_loading
description: Continues record loading from a saved index, matching the key word against stored entries and writing field values for the remaining entries before returning.

name: write_record_fields_per_entry
description: For each record from one up to the stored count, writes an offset word, several byte fields, a flag taken from bit seven of one byte, and two bit-packed fields from consecutive bytes.

name: write_record_fields_until_count
description: Writes the per-record fields for each entry in turn, clearing a status byte and setting its top flag bit as needed, and stops once the stored entry count is passed.

name: select_entry_and_reset_slots
description: Selects an entry index from the argument byte, mapping values of 128 or more through a lookup table. It initialises the entry's slot through a routine when the slot is empty, sets its active flag, and zeroes the long-word slots from the stored starting index up to 256.

name: zero_slots_from_start_index
description: Sets a flag byte to one, zeroes the long-word slots from a stored starting index up to 256, and makes one call.

name: clear_slots_from_stored_index
description: Zeroes the long-word slots from a stored starting index up to 256 using a do-while loop, then makes one call. It is the loop form of a sibling routine that first sets a flag byte.

name: init_slot_if_empty
description: Checks the long slot indexed by the low word of the argument and, when that slot is zero, calls a routine and stores a value from the state block into it.

name: register_pending_entry_998
description: When a pending long in the state block is non-zero, obtains a new entry index through a routine and fills its type byte with two, its word with 998, its flag with one and its long with the pending value. It clears three further bytes for that index, then makes a call, and calls a routine with zeros when a second flag word is set.

name: register_pending_entry_999
description: Performs the same registration as its sibling for a different pending long, filling the entry's word with 999 instead of 998. It also calls a routine with zeros when a third flag word is set.

name: format_value_digits_with_cache
description: When the argument changes it resets the display state, then reuses a cached slot for values below 900 or formats the value as three decimal digit characters and passes that text to a routine. A tens and units pair taken from a table byte is written before the lookup on the cached path.

name: clear_cached_slots_if_flagged
description: When a flag word is non-zero, it zeroes every entry of the slot table that is not the sentinel minus one, covering the number of entries stored in the state block.

name: populate_slots_from_list
description: Calls two setup routines, then reads a count and repeatedly reads a slot index. Unset slots receive a call to a routine, and set slots are overwritten with the value returned by another routine, counting down until the count is used up.

name: draw_numbered_status_line
description: Chooses a character from a table, or uses the value one for arguments of 900 and above, and prints it as a status line. The first five calls use one text template and later calls use another, while a counter in the state block advances each time.

name: run_code_sequence_check
description: Makes a call chosen from two state values, then repeatedly makes calls and reads codes. It returns one when a flag is set, and returns zero when the codes break the expected pattern of one followed by two, or two followed by one, with at most one repeat.

name: parse_resource_header_fields
description: Reads a sequence of 32-bit and 16-bit values from the loaded data, with an optional tag check that adds a further value. It stores the entry count, four table pointers and several offsets into the state block, then sets a status word to one.

name: load_resource_tables
description: Reads a header of counts and an optional tag check, then fills several tables from the loaded data. For each entry it stores a byte and a long into parallel arrays, and for the last table it stores three bytes plus one byte per record. It ends by setting a status word to one.

name: clear_resource_tables
description: Resets the parallel tables for the counted entries, setting the flag bytes of the first table to one, then zeroes two byte regions of 796 and 199 bytes and clears the long and flag tables for the second count.

name: record_unrecovered_routine_body
description: No pseudo-code is available for this routine, so its behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence. The facts show 45 instructions, two callers and six callees.

name: store_record_or_retry_countdown
description: Reads a value and, when a status is zero, stores a pointer in the state block and copies two state bytes into the record it points to, returning zero. Otherwise it decrements a retry counter and, when that reaches zero, resets it to five and makes several calls, returning one.

name: get_status_word
description: Returns the status word stored in the state block without changing any state.

name: read_buffer_xor_status_byte
description: Reads one value into a small buffer and stores, as a status word, whether that read returned a value other than one. It returns the four buffer bytes, each XORed with a state byte.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero and performs no other work.

name: stub_no_operation_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: read_pair_xor_status_byte
description: Reads a two-byte value into a small buffer and stores, as a status word, whether that read returned a value other than one. It returns the two buffer bytes, each XORed with a state byte.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes decode as bad instruction data rather than real code, so the routine has no recoverable behaviour.

name: read_byte_through_pointer
description: Reads and returns the byte at the address passed as its argument.

name: clear_status_word
description: Sets the status word in the state block to zero and does nothing else.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes decode as bad instruction data rather than real code, so the routine has no recoverable behaviour.

name: fill_identity_index_tables
description: Fills two 32-entry word tables so that each entry holds its own index.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes decode as bad instruction data rather than real code, so the routine has no recoverable behaviour.

name: decrement_counted_slot_entries
description: While a countdown byte in the state block is non-zero, it steps the countdown down and, unless the looked-up table entry is 255, decrements the count byte for that entry in a per-entry table.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero and performs no other work.

name: read_word_xor_status_byte
description: Calls a routine for a word value, sets the status word to one when that value is 65535 and to zero otherwise, and returns the value XORed with a state byte.

name: update_scroll_direction_state
description: Compares the current and target positions and sets a direction byte to two or one when they differ by one step of eight. Otherwise it resets the state and runs a routine for each of 40 entries, and it also calls routines for flagged entries when the position differs.

name: mark_slot_flag_and_call
description: Clears a status word, sets the high bit of the slot flag at the argument offset within the current block, and records that offset and a flag. It finishes with one call computed from a pending long.

name: compute_slot_bounds_and_offsets
description: Computes the base pointer for a slot from a table, widens the stored minimum and maximum bounds with the current entry's values, and derives offsets from fixed base values and a 64-byte row stride. For each further entry in the count it repeats the calculation with a second offset.

name: read_next_code_byte
description: Reads the next byte from a stream pointer and advances it. It returns that byte offset by minus ten, or the result of a further call when the byte was ten.

name: clear_state_flag_byte
description: Clears a one-byte flag in the state block.

name: decode_run_length_rows_stride
description: Decodes a packed run-length stream into eight passes of rows with a stride of 320 bytes. It takes literal values from a 16-entry table, and a control bit selects fill values instead when a flag is set.

name: decode_run_length_rows_restructured
description: Performs the same run-length row decoding as its sibling, written with a restructured loop, writing values at a 320-byte row stride until the pass counter is exhausted.

name: decode_run_length_seeded
description: Starts a run-length decode from a register-held byte and writes the decoded values down a buffer at a 320-byte row stride, reading the packed stream until the pass counter is exhausted.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes decode as bad instruction data rather than real code, so the routine has no recoverable behaviour.

name: reset_display_arrays
description: Calls one routine with a stored word and sets a state byte to one. It then clears 40 bytes of one table and sets 20 words of a second table to 200.

name: decode_run_length_columns
description: Decodes a packed run-length stream into an output buffer with a 320-byte row stride across several passes, handling repeat codes and literal runs. A final loop copies pairs of long words into a second buffer, skipping columns flagged in a 40-byte table.

name: decode_run_length_stride_forty
description: Decodes a packed run-length stream of one-byte values into a destination written every 40 bytes until a total count is used up. A control byte with its high bit clear copies that many following bytes, and with the high bit set it repeats the next byte.

name: reset_display_arrays_alt
description: Makes a call with a stored word, sets a state byte to one, clears 40 bytes of one table, and sets 20 words of a second table to 200. It matches its sibling except for the routine it calls first.

name: clear_pending_count
description: Sets the pending byte count in the state block to zero.

name: append_pending_byte
description: Stores the high byte of the argument at the end of a pending byte buffer and advances its count. Once the count passes 70 it calls a routine with the buffer address.

name: copy_indexed_entries_to_table
description: For each active entry up to the stored count, copies a byte from a source table at the index held in an index word into a destination table at that entry's position.

name: find_matching_entry_for_range
description: Looks up a mask word for the high part of the argument and scans 13 entries, returning the first entry whose mask overlaps it, whose flag bit is clear, and whose byte range covers the argument's low word. Returns zero when no entry matches.

name: scan_entries_mask_range
description: Scans 13 entries for the first one whose mask word overlaps the argument mask, whose flag bit is clear, and whose byte range covers the value in the argument. Returns that index, or zero when no entry matches.

name: find_next_matching_entry
description: Searches entries one to twelve for one whose mask word overlaps the given mask, whose flag bit is clear, and whose byte range covers the argument value. It returns that index, or zero when the search passes the last entry.

name: walk_linked_entries_downward
description: Walks the entry list downward from the stored entry count. For each entry whose flag nibble is set it follows a link table to the next entry, calling a routine when the link ends at zero, until the count is exhausted.

name: flush_pending_byte_buffer
description: For each non-zero byte in the pending buffer it stores the byte and calls a routine, then resets the pending count to zero.

name: mark_entries_in_range
description: Looks up the bounds of the current entry from the state tables and, for each position in that range that fits the mode byte, sets bit six of its flag. It also stores two shifted values and calls a routine with the computed offset.

name: copy_entry_block_bytes
description: Locates the data block for the given entry and writes two table bytes for it, followed by two zero bytes. It then copies the rest of the block, up to its count word, into the output.

name: copy_stream_bytes_to_buffer
description: Copies a counted number of bytes from the current stream pointer into the destination buffer, advancing both pointers as it goes.

name: clear_frame_tables
description: Resets several per-entry tables: it sets the first table to one for its count, zeroes the second table, clears a 200-byte table, and for the entries in two ranges calls a routine on any non-zero slot before clearing it.

name: dispatch_by_mode_byte
description: Selects an action from a mode byte. Modes one and two each pass the value to the same routine, mode three adds the value to a state byte, and any other mode returns the mode minus three.

name: forward_call_wrapper_one
description: Makes one call to another routine and returns, adding nothing else.

name: forward_call_wrapper_two
description: Makes one call to another routine and returns, adding nothing else. It is a second copy of its sibling wrapper.

name: add_word_to_state_byte
description: Adds the low byte of a word from the caller's frame to a state byte.

name: process_in_16k_blocks
description: Repeats a call on consecutive chunks of at most 16384 bytes until the requested byte count is used up, advancing the pointer by each chunk.

name: forward_with_state_handle
description: Passes the stored state handle and the argument to another routine, then returns.

name: xor_mask_bytes_and_send
description: XORs two bytes of the argument with a state byte. When a check routine returns zero it sends the first of them through a library call, sets the status word from the result, and advances a counter by two.

name: clear_flags_keep_top
description: Zeroes two state words and a countdown byte, then keeps only the top bit of each of 200 flag bytes, clearing the rest.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes decode as bad instruction data rather than real code, so the routine has no recoverable behaviour.

name: unpack_three_byte_records
description: Divides a stored length by three to get a record count. For each three-byte record it builds a 12-bit value from three nibbles and passes it to a routine with the record index, with a second pass that repeats this only for records whose stored word differs from the cached one.

name: call_with_stored_handle
description: Passes the stored state handle to another routine and returns.

name: read_little_endian_long
description: Reads four bytes from the pointer and assembles them into a 32-bit value, with the first byte as the lowest byte.

name: xor_decode_buffer_chunks
description: Reads a byte count in chunks of at most 16384, calls a routine to fill the buffer for each chunk, and XORs every byte of the buffer with a state byte.

name: copy_c_string
description: Copies bytes from the source string into the destination, advancing both pointers, and stops after writing the terminating zero byte.

name: copy_and_place_text_line
description: Copies its argument into a 100-byte local buffer, then makes two calls with positions derived from a state word and fixed offsets, one of them using a fixed value and the other the computed offset.

name: run_frame_state_machine
description: Copies thirteen state bytes and sets up fourteen rectangle positions from table values, then reads a key code and branches on it. Code eight, thirteen and fourteen each make their own calls, code twelve clears a range of 40-byte entries and returns, and codes ten and eleven set a state value to one or two. The pseudo-code is truncated partway through, so the later branches are not described.

name: store_indexed_rect_record
description: Stores a rectangle record at the index given by the first argument. It writes two corner words, two extents made absolute when negative, a long value and several attribute bytes into per-index tables.

name: place_indexed_items_by_state
description: Resets twenty index words to minus one, then for a state value of zero makes four placement calls around a computed centre position. For states one or two it makes two placement calls plus nine calls for indexed entries.

name: draw_state_dependent_frame
description: Makes a sequence of calls positioned from a state word. One set of fixed values is used when the state is zero, another when the state is one or two, and a final call is made when the index word is non-zero.

name: render_indexed_rect_entry
description: Renders a stored rectangle record when its first word is not minus one. It draws either a filled or an outlined rectangle depending on a flag byte, then makes further calls that use the record's attribute and a computed offset.

name: find_rect_containing_point
description: Scans up to 20 rectangle records and returns the index of the first active one whose horizontal and vertical bounds contain the point given by the argument, or minus one when none matches.

name: record_unrecovered_routine_body
description: No pseudo-code is available for this routine, so its behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence. The facts show 18 instructions and two callers.

name: adjust_coordinate_differences
description: Turns two negative fields of the second argument into absolute differences from the first argument, then makes four calls that pair coordinates from both arguments.

name: set_flag_and_call_routine
description: Sets a one-byte state flag to one and then makes one call to another routine.

name: select_handle_by_slot_number
description: When the word argument is one or two, looks up a state value at one of two fixed offsets using the argument and stores it as the state handle. For other values it leaves the handle unchanged.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes decode as bad instruction data rather than real code, so the routine has no recoverable behaviour.

name: load_record_header_and_words
description: Loads a 38-byte record for the index given by the argument. It copies its first bytes and a further four bytes into state, stores the high word of the argument as a status byte, clears a counter, then fills 16 words from the record as big-endian values.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes decode as bad instruction data rather than real code, so the routine has no recoverable behaviour.

name: release_resources_and_clear_flag
description: Clears a pending word and calls a library routine when it was set, then runs another routine. It calls a further library routine when a flag byte is clear, clears that flag, and makes several more library calls.

name: forward_call_wrapper_three
description: Makes one call to another routine and returns, adding nothing else.

name: fill_bytes_with_value
description: Writes the byte value from the second argument into consecutive bytes of the destination, repeating for the count held in the argument's high word, and returns the destination pointer.

name: release_stored_handle
description: If the stored state handle is non-zero, passes it to another routine and then clears the handle.

name: forward_parameter_to_routine
description: Passes its single parameter straight to another routine and returns.

name: release_indexed_slot
description: Looks up the slot for the word argument in a table with four-byte entries. When the slot holds a non-zero value it passes that value to another routine and clears the slot.

name: record_unrecovered_routine_body
description: No pseudo-code is available for this routine, so its behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence. The facts show 22 instructions, four callers and two callees.

name: search_entries_for_threshold
description: Steps through a list by calling a routine until an entry value is at or above the argument. If nothing qualifies it repeats the search with a state flag set, and when still nothing qualifies it calls routines for a fallback entry.

name: pop_highest_priority_entry
description: Scans the entry table for the non-zero entry with the largest priority byte, skipping priorities of 127 or more unless a state flag is set. It clears that entry, passes its stored value to a routine, and returns whether an entry was found.

name: pop_first_eligible_entry
description: Finds the first non-zero entry whose flag byte has its low seven bits clear, whose priority is under 127 unless a state flag is set, and which is not the excluded index. It clears that entry, passes its value to a routine and returns one, or zero when none qualifies.

name: pop_first_free_entry
description: Walks the first entry table from its start to its end pointer and takes the first non-zero entry whose flag byte has its low seven bits clear and whose priority is under 127 unless a state flag is set. It clears that entry, passes its value to a routine and returns one, or zero if none qualifies.

name: pop_first_eligible_second_table
description: Scans the second entry table in the same way as its sibling, clearing and passing on the first non-zero entry whose flag low bits are clear and whose priority is under 127 unless a state flag is set.

name: cycle_through_four_states
description: Steps a small state counter through the values zero to three, calling a routine for each state and recording its result. It returns one as soon as a result is non-zero, and zero when the counter comes back to its start value.

name: swap_long_word_byte_order
description: Reverses the byte order of a 32-bit value, moving its lowest byte to the top and its highest byte to the bottom.

name: index_records_by_type
description: Walks a block of variable-length records. Types one to six store the record pointer in a table slot indexed by the record's byte, while any other type is passed to a routine, and the walk advances by each record's size.

name: find_largest_slot_total
description: For each slot in a fixed table, sums a routine's result over a linked list of entries whose pointers lie within a bound, then returns the largest total found.

name: split_free_block_and_link
description: Links a block into a free list. When fewer than eight bytes would be left over it links the whole block, otherwise it splits off the remainder as a new block with its size set and links that instead.

name: copy_longs_by_byte_count
description: Copies 32-bit values from the source to the destination, decreasing a byte count by four per value until the count is no longer positive.

name: check_range_for_marked_record
description: Walks records in a byte range and returns one when it reaches a type-six record whose table flag has any of its low seven bits set. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: compact_block_list_entries
description: Walks a linked list of blocks below a bound, calling routines to copy each block to a new offset, then updating its stored size and link fields. A flag word is set to one while a copy runs and cleared afterwards.

name: find_free_block_of_size
description: Refreshes the free list entries from a table, then walks the free list for the first block whose size is at least the argument and splits it out through a routine. It returns zero when no block fits.

name: allocate_rounded_block
description: Rounds the requested size up to a multiple of eight, with a minimum of eight, then walks the free list for the first block large enough and takes it. When no block fits it requests a new block through a routine.

name: free_block_and_merge_neighbours
description: Inserts a block into the address-sorted free list, sizes it with a routine, then merges it with the following block and the preceding block when they are adjacent.

name: truncate_result_to_word
description: Calls a routine with its argument and returns the result truncated to a 16-bit signed value.

name: probe_and_allocate_memory_pool
description: Uses the Amiga exec AllocMem and FreeMem calls to probe available memory with trial allocations, halving a step from 262144 bytes. It keeps up to ten regions larger than 20000 bytes, sorts them by size and links them into a free list, returning one, or zero when a required allocation fails.

name: allocate_sized_block_with_header
description: Releases any block already held in the state pointer, then allocates a block two bytes larger than the argument. It stores that size in the first word and returns the address after it, or zero when the argument is zero or allocation fails.

name: software_divide_longs
description: Divides two 32-bit register operands in software, negating for negative inputs and normalising the divisor before computing the result, with a separate path when the divisor fits in 16 bits.

name: store_block_pointer_minus_two
description: When its argument is non-zero, makes a call and stores the argument minus two in the state block as the held pointer. It then returns zero.

name: multiply_long_values
description: Multiplies two 32-bit register operands using 16-bit partial products, combining the cross products into the high half of the result.

name: poll_until_state_change
description: Clears a flag word and calls a routine repeatedly until a state word becomes non-zero or the flag is set. It returns that state word, with one extra call when the state equals three.

name: handle_input_state_transitions
description: Updates a cursor position from a computed horizontal range, then branches on the current state code. Some codes draw fixed sets of entries, code four toggles a pending flag, and code eighteen flips a toggle and draws one of two labels. The plus, minus, equals and underscore codes adjust a counter clamped between zero and nine, and other codes fill a ten-byte text buffer.

name: increment_hold_counter
description: Increments a hold counter. When it was zero it sets a flag, makes a call and saves a stored value, then makes one further call.

name: decrement_hold_counter
description: Decrements a hold counter. When it reaches zero or below it clears the counter and the flag, makes a call and restores a saved value, then makes one further call.

name: copy_entry_string_to_buffer
description: Copies the zero-terminated string stored in the indexed table entry into a fixed buffer in the state block and terminates it.

name: run_prompt_until_key_code
description: When a state pointer is unset it makes one of two calls depending on a flag and returns zero. Otherwise it sets up display values from its arguments, makes calls, then loops reading a key code until a non-zero code is stored, returning the pair of results.

name: update_selected_text_entry
description: When its argument is non-zero it reads the stored key code for the current entry, clears that entry, makes display calls and compares the key code with the previous one. Otherwise it makes a fixed set of calls and returns.

name: clear_entry_key_and_refresh
description: Reads a key code from the current text entry, clears it, and makes calls to refresh the display. It makes one more call when the state code matches the key code or the key code plus 32.

name: compare_strings_ordering
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings byte by byte, returning zero when they are identical, one when the first is greater, and minus one when the first is smaller.

name: clear_flag_with_call
description: When the flag byte is set it makes one call, then clears the flag.

name: stub_empty_return_body
description: Contains only a return, so calling it performs no work.

name: read_code_into_state
description: Clears a flag word, stores the result of one routine call as a code word in the state block, makes a library call, and returns that code word.

name: pop_ring_buffer_entry
description: Makes a library call, then, when the read index differs from the write index, returns the entry at the read index, clears that slot and advances the index modulo 16. It returns zero when the buffer is empty.

name: measure_string_length
description: Returns the number of bytes before the zero terminator of the argument string.

name: stub_return_no_work
description: Contains only a return, so calling it performs no work.

name: handle_code_seven_selection
description: When the state code equals seven it looks up two entries from a table with a library call, stores a pair of values into the state block, makes display calls and sets the update flag, then returns zero. When the code is 21 it makes one call and returns zero, and for any other code it returns one.

name: restore_saved_state_on_countdown
description: Decrements a countdown word and, when it reaches zero, writes a saved value into a linked structure, copies twenty bytes of saved state into a second block, and makes three library calls.

name: fill_byte_run_from_argument
description: Writes the byte from the argument into the destination for a count held in the argument's high word, advancing the destination pointer as it goes.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes decode as bad instruction data rather than real code, so the routine has no recoverable behaviour.

name: clear_flag_and_call_library
description: Clears the one-byte flag in the state block and makes one library call.

name: increment_counter_and_notify
description: Increments a counter word in the state block and makes one call when the counter has just become one.

name: wait_for_nonzero_result
description: Repeatedly calls a routine until its result has a non-zero low word, then returns that result.

name: draw_line_between_points
description: Computes the absolute deltas between two points, then steps along the major axis with an error accumulator, making a routine call each time the minor coordinate moves.

name: set_word_reset_if_zero
description: Stores the argument word in a state word, with minus one replaced by zero and not stored in the first word, and stores it again in a second state word. It makes one call when the stored value is zero.

name: store_pointer_and_return_pair
description: Stores the first long of its pointer argument at the location named by another long in that block, and returns a value pair in which a zero word has been replaced by one.

name: set_flag_with_branch_calls
description: Makes one call, then makes three further calls when the state flag is clear or two when it is set, and sets the flag to one.

name: mark_code_two_entries
description: Clears a 20-entry flag table and sets the current index to minus one. For each entry whose code byte is two and is still unmarked, it records that entry as current and makes three calls.

name: read_next_stream_byte
description: Returns the next byte from the stream pointer and advances the pointer by one.

name: read_next_stream_word
description: Reads the next two bytes from the stream as a little-endian 16-bit word and advances the stream pointer by two.

name: dispatch_stream_commands
description: Repeatedly reads a command byte from the stream until the current index is minus one. For each command it saves the stream position, marks the entry, and calls a handler taken from a table indexed by that byte.

name: run_active_slot_three_steps
description: When the current slot index is not minus one, makes three calls to other routines in sequence.

name: load_slot_value_into_pointer
description: When the current slot index is set, loads the value stored for that slot plus a base offset into a pointer variable in the state block.

name: save_pointer_into_slot
description: When the current slot index is set, stores the pointer variable minus a base offset back into that slot's table entry.

name: run_two_routine_calls
description: Makes two calls to other routines in sequence and returns.

name: resolve_slot_by_type
description: For the current slot index, resolves a value according to its type byte. Type two reads or looks up a cached value from tables, possibly searching an entry list through a routine. Type one copies a stored value, and type zero searches a list for a matching key. Other types call a routine. Unless it returns early, it clears the slot's flag and marks the current index as unset.

name: clear_type_one_two_entries
description: Loops over twenty entries and clears the state byte of those with type one, and of those with type two whose threshold word is at least the mode byte. A routine call precedes each clear when a related flag is set.

name: clear_typed_entries_loop
description: Performs the same type-one and type-two entry clearing as its sibling, written as a do-while loop over twenty entries.

name: release_entries_matching_key
description: For a key byte, clears every active type-two entry whose slot word matches the key, resetting the current index when it pointed to one of them. It then marks matching entries in a second list as released.

name: release_untyped_entries_by_key
description: For a key word, clears active entries of type zero or one whose slot word matches the key, resetting the current index when it pointed to one of them. It then marks matching entries in a second list as released.

name: release_untyped_entries_loop
description: Performs the same release by key as its sibling for type zero or one entries, looping over twenty entries and then the second list in one pass.

name: mark_second_list_entries_released
description: Walks the second list up to its count and, for each entry whose key word matches the argument, sets the key to minus one, marks its state byte as released and records the index.

name: push_slot_into_second_list
description: Adds the current slot to the second list by storing its key word and state byte at the end and incrementing the count. It then makes calls, resumes the newest entry with two calls when its check passes, and otherwise clears the current index.

name: record_unrecovered_routine_body
description: No pseudo-code is available for this routine, so its behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence. The facts show 90 instructions, four callers and five callees.

name: find_free_slot_index
description: Scans slot flags from one to nineteen for the first clear entry and returns its index. When none is free it makes a call with a fixed base offset and returns that call's result.

name: mark_entries_bump_counters
description: Sets the high bit of every other active entry whose restriction byte is clear or whose argument exceeds 127, increments six per-class counters, and clears the high bit of the entry recorded as pending.

name: mark_active_entries_loop_variant
description: Performs the same entry marking and six-counter update as its sibling, written as a loop that handles the entries first and then the counters.

name: bump_counters_clear_pending
description: Increments six per-class counters, then clears the high bit of the pending entry and resets that entry's secondary byte.

name: decrement_countdowns_and_expire
description: For each entry in state one, subtracts the argument's high word from its countdown long. When the countdown falls below that amount it sets the entry's state to two and zeroes the countdown.

name: render_text_on_range_check
description: When the second argument's low word is below its high word, or the third argument's low word is below the second's low word, copies the first argument into a 100-byte buffer and makes three calls with it, using a fixed offset and the second argument.

name: forward_three_args_with_buffer
description: Passes its three arguments to another routine together with a fixed buffer offset, then makes two more calls using that offset and the stored state.
